data.claim: An unknown author still has exactly one family, so reviewers from two or more distinct families necessarily include one outside it; reviewer independence should satisfy on such a clean cross-family panel.
data.falsifier: A single-family panel under an unknown author is still refused (cannot be shown to differ).
data.mechanism: Record the panel's reviewer families on the review evidence; a panel spanning >=2 distinct families is accepted when the author's family is unresolvable (not a router).
data.probe: Regression test: unknown author + grok/gemini panel => tier family; single-family panel => none.
data.question: Does reviewer independence block completion when the author has no session model, even though grok (xai) and gemini (google) reviewed clean and are cross-family to each other?

evidence.note: Research R-b1a30dc3303-unknown-author-cross-family (CONFIRMED): recorded reviewer families on review evidence; unknown author + >=2-family panel satisfies independence. Probe: regression test added and passing; single-family panel still refused.

chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback claims to name a reviewer from a “minority” family when `review_tier` cannot identify a cross-family reviewer, but it never checks that the family chosen by `Counter(...).most_common(1)[0][0]` is strictly more common than the others. For tied results ordered `[gemini, grok]` with both `REVIEWED` and the unknown author actually belonging to the `grok` family, `review_tier` returns no cross reviewer; `familias` is `["gemini", "grok"]`, `majority` is `"gemini"` because it appears first, and the loop returns the `grok` reviewer. That is the same-family reviewer, not the clean cross-family one, so the function still names the wrong reviewer in exactly the situation the fix is supposed to solve. The condition should require a strict majority before treating the remaining family as “minority”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:_identifying_reviewer (fallback tie-break)

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion is vacuous for the bug it is meant to regress: `ok, why = G.reviewer_independence(...); assert ok, why`. On the unfixed code, an unknown author reaches the unchanged `return "none", why` path shown in this same diff, so `ok` is the non-empty string `"none"`, which is truthy. Thus the test would pass even before the fix, so it does not fail on B1a30dc3303 and does not guard the change. It should assert the pass status explicitly, such as `ok == "family"`, rather than relying on string truthiness.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_identifying_reviewer.py:test_an_unknown_author_accepts_a_clean_cross_family_panel

chunk_findings.detail: When the author model is unknown, `review_tier` never marks a tied reviewer as cross-family, so the new branch runs. `Counter.most_common(1)` treats the first family among equal counts, or the largest count, as the one to avoid. Input: tied clean results `[family=google, family=cursor, family=google]` and an unknown author whose real family is cursor (one same-family pass plus two google-family passes). Majority is `google`, so the function returns the cursor reviewer — the same-family name bug B1a30dc3303 says must not win — and the docstring's "most likely cross-family" claim is false for that panel. Equal counts with the cross-family reviewer first (`[grok, cursor]`) do the same: first family becomes "majority" and the same-family reviewer is named.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review/run.py:328

chunk_findings.detail: The test treats two single-family records on different gates as one cross-family panel. Given critic evidence only `{family: "xai"}` and rubber_duck evidence only `{family: "google"}`, it requires `independence_tier == "family"` and `reviewer_independence` success for author `""`. That input never places two families on the same review, so it accepts a critic review that the sibling test says must stay `"none"`, as long as another gate was reviewed by a different family. It also injects evidence through `G.record`, so it stays green if attribution still drops a clean cross-family reviewer. `test_an_unknown_author_accepts_a_clean_cross_family_panel` does not close that hole: `ev["family"] in ("xai", "google")` is true when only one of the two clean reviewers is kept.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reviewer_independence_soft.py:test_an_unknown_author_with_a_cross_family_panel_is_independent
